newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: US, EU criticise Ecuador's compliance with WTO.
newsitem.headline: US, EU criticise Ecuador's compliance with WTO.

text.p: Ecuador, which joined the World Trade Organisation (WTO) a year ago, came under fire on Friday from the United States and European Union who accused it of not living up to all of its WTO commitments, trade sources said.
The Ecuadorean delegation, in an oral report, defended Quito's record but conceded there had been some shortcomings in implenting the terms of the accession protocol, they added.
The debate was held at a closed-door General Council of the WTO. Ecuador joined the 130-member watchdog in January 1996.

Trade sources quoted the U.S. trade delegation as saying that despite a limited transition period for Ecuador, a number of barriers to imports remained in effect which the United States characterised as violating the accession protocol.

These were: a special consumption tax which Washington argued discriminated against imported goods; import restrictions on used tires, cars and clothing; technical standards for health and safety which the U.S. argued were not being applied judiciously; import licenses for agricultural and other products which according to the Americans have been used to keep goods out of the market; and alleged failure to implement the trade- related aspects of intellectual property rights accord (TRIPS).
"The EU echoed the U.S. criticism," a trade source said.
Ecuador's team replied that the consumption tax was applied equally to domestic and imported goods, while health and environmental measures had to remain intact, trade sources said.
"They conceded there were some problems in implementing all aspects of it (the accession protocol), but said they were moving in the general direction," a trade source said.
"(They said that) with regard to certain things, including the restrictions on the used goods that these were in no way unique and were being used by many other WTO members."
Venezuela, speaking also for Colombia, supported Ecuador with respect to TRIPS, they added. Ecuador was in line with the intellectual property provisions of the Andean trade pact.
New Zealand stressed the importance of implementing commitments in the protocol, while Switzerland complained about Ecuador's TRIPS regime, according to trade sources.
